completeMatchedUnits.zh: 於是使尚書和郁等持節詣東宮，廢太子為庶人，太子改服出，再拜受詔，步出承華門，乘粗犢車，車武公澹以兵仗送太子及妃王氏、三子虨、臧、尚同幽於金墉城。
completeMatchedUnits.en: He Yu of the Masters of Writing and others were sent with credentials to the Eastern Palace. The heir apparent changed his garments, bowed twice, received the edict, walked out through the Chenghua Gate, and rode a rough ox-cart. Sima Dan, Duke of Dongwu, escorted him with armed guards, together with his consort Lady Wang and his three sons Bin, Zang, and Shang, to confinement at Jinyong.
completeMatchedUnits.literal: Thereupon He Yu of the Masters of Writing and others were sent with credentials to the Eastern Palace to depose the Heir Apparent as commoner. The Heir Apparent changed his garments and came out, bowed twice and received the edict, walked out through the Chenghua Gate, rode a rough ox-cart, and the Duke of Dongwu, Sima Dan, with arms escorted the Heir Apparent, his consort Lady Wang, and his three sons Bin, Zang, and Shang together to be confined at Jinyong.

completeMatchedUnits.zh: 詔以黃門首辭班示公卿，遣東武公澹以千兵防衛太子，幽於許昌宮，令持書御史劉振持節守之，詔宮臣不得辭送。
completeMatchedUnits.en: An edict showed the confession to the ministers, sent Sima Dan, Marquis of Dongwu, with a thousand troops to guard the heir apparent at Xuchang Palace, and ordered Liu Zhen, Attendant Secretary with credentials, to hold him under guard, forbidding palace officials to escort him on departure.
completeMatchedUnits.literal: An edict displayed the Yellow Gate confessor's testimony to the excellencies and ministers, dispatched the Marquis of Dongwu Sima Dan with a thousand troops to guard the Heir Apparent, confined him at the Xuchang palace, ordered the Attendant Secretary with credentials Liu Zhen to hold him under guard, and decreed that palace officials might not take leave to escort him.

fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.zh: 賈后使董猛矯以長廣公主辭白帝曰：「事宜速決，而群臣各不同，其不從詔者，宜以軍法從事。」
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.en: Empress Jia had Dong Meng report to the emperor in the name of the Princess of Changguang: "This must be decided at once. The ministers are divided. Those who disobey the edict should be dealt with by military law."
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.literal: Empress Jia had Dong Meng, falsely in the name of the Princess of Changguang, report to the emperor: "The affair ought to be decided quickly, yet the ministers all differ; those who do not follow the edict ought to be handled by military law."

fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.zh: 議至日西，不決。
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.en: Debate continued until sunset without resolution.
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.literal: Deliberation continued until the sun was in the west, without decision.

fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.zh: 后見華等意堅，懼事變，乃表免太子為庶人，詔許之。
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.en: Seeing Zhang Hua and the others hold firm and fearing the plot might fail, the empress memorialized to depose the heir apparent as a commoner. The edict was approved.
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.literal: The empress, seeing that Hua and the others were firm in intent and fearing the affair might change, submitted a memorial to depose the Heir Apparent as commoner; an edict approved it.

fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.zh: 於是使尚書和郁等持節詣東宮，廢太子為庶人，太子改服出，再拜受詔，步出承華門，乘粗犢車，車武公澹以兵仗送太子及妃王氏、三子虨、臧、尚同幽於金墉城。
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.en: He Yu of the Masters of Writing and others were sent with credentials to the Eastern Palace. The heir apparent changed his garments, bowed twice, received the edict, walked out through the Chenghua Gate, and rode a rough ox-cart. Sima Dan, Duke of Dongwu, escorted him with armed guards, together with his consort Lady Wang and his three sons Bin, Zang, and Shang, to confinement at Jinyong.
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.literal: Thereupon He Yu of the Masters of Writing and others were sent with credentials to the Eastern Palace to depose the Heir Apparent as commoner. The Heir Apparent changed his garments and came out, bowed twice and received the edict, walked out through the Chenghua Gate, rode a rough ox-cart, and the Duke of Dongwu, Sima Dan, with arms escorted the Heir Apparent, his consort Lady Wang, and his three sons Bin, Zang, and Shang together to be confined at Jinyong.

fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.zh: 王衍自表離婚，許之，妃慟哭而歸。
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.en: Wang Yan memorialized to divorce her, and permission was granted. The consort returned home in bitter tears.
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.literal: Wang Yan himself submitted a memorial requesting divorce; it was granted, and the consort returned home weeping bitterly.

fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.zh: 殺太子母謝淑媛及虨母保林蔣俊。
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.en: The heir apparent's mother, Lady Xie the Gracious Lady, and Bin's mother, Jiang Jun, a consort of baolin rank, were executed.
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.literal: The Heir Apparent's mother, the Gracious Lady Xie, and Bin's mother, Jiang Jun, a consort of baolin rank, were killed.

fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.zh: 賈后使黃門自首欲與太子為逆。
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.en: Empress Jia had a Yellow Gate attendant confess a plot to rebel with the heir apparent.
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.literal: Empress Jia had a Yellow Gate attendant confess that he wished to rebel with the Heir Apparent.

fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.zh: 詔以黃門首辭班示公卿，遣東武公澹以千兵防衛太子，幽於許昌宮，令持書御史劉振持節守之，詔宮臣不得辭送。
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.en: An edict showed the confession to the ministers, sent Sima Dan, Marquis of Dongwu, with a thousand troops to guard the heir apparent at Xuchang Palace, and ordered Liu Zhen, Attendant Secretary with credentials, to hold him under guard, forbidding palace officials to escort him on departure.
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.literal: An edict displayed the Yellow Gate confessor's testimony to the excellencies and ministers, dispatched the Marquis of Dongwu Sima Dan with a thousand troops to guard the Heir Apparent, confined him at the Xuchang palace, ordered the Attendant Secretary with credentials Liu Zhen to hold him under guard, and decreed that palace officials might not take leave to escort him.

fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.zh: 洗馬江統、潘滔、舍人王敦、杜蕤、魯瑤等冒禁至伊水，拜辭涕泣。
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.en: Jiang Tong, Pan Tao, Wang Dun, Du Rui, Lu Yao, and others defied the ban, went to the Yi River, bowed farewell, and wept.
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.literal: The Groom Jiang Tong, Pan Tao, Attendant Wang Dun, Du Rui, Lu Yao, and others braved the prohibition to reach the Yi River, bowed in farewell, and wept.

fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.zh: 司隸校尉滿奮收縛統籌送獄。
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.en: Colonel of the Censorate Man Fen arrested Tong and the others and sent them to prison.
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.literal: The Colonel of the Censorate Man Fen arrested and bound Tong and his companions and sent them to prison.

fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.zh: 其系河南獄者，樂廣悉解遣之；
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.en: Those held in the Henan prison were all released by Yue Guang;
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.literal: Those held in the Henan prison were all released by Yue Guang;

fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.zh: 系洛陽縣獄者，猶未釋。
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.en: those held in the Luoyang county prison were not yet released.
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.literal: those held in the Luoyang county prison were still not released.

fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.zh: 都官從事孫琰說賈謐曰：「所以廢徙太子，以其為惡故耳。
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.en: Director of Justice Sun Yan told Jia Mi: "The heir apparent was deposed because he was wicked.
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.literal: Director of Justice Sun Yan said to Jia Mi: "The reason for deposing and relocating the Heir Apparent is that he was wicked.

fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.zh: 今宮臣冒罪拜辭，而加以重辟；
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.en: Yet you would punish palace officials who came to bid him farewell;
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.literal: Now palace officials offend the law to bid farewell; yet you add heavy punishment;

fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.zh: 流聞四方，乃更彰太子之德也，不如釋之。」
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.en: If word spreads abroad it will only highlight the heir apparent's virtue. Better release them."
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.literal: if this spreads to the four quarters it will only make the Heir Apparent's virtue more manifest—better to release them."

fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.zh: 謐乃語洛陽令曹攄使釋之；
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.en: Mi then told Cao Shu, Magistrate of Luoyang, to release them;
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.literal: Mi thereupon told the Magistrate of Luoyang Cao Shu to release them;

fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.zh: 廣亦不坐。
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.en: Guang was not punished either.
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.literal: Guang was also not punished.

fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.zh: 敦，覽之孫；
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.en: Dun was the grandson of Wang Lan;
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.literal: Dun was the grandson of Wang Lan;

fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.zh: 攄，肇之孫也。
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.en: Shu was the grandson of Cao Zhao.
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.literal: Shu was the grandson of Cao Zhao.

fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.zh: 太子至許，遺王妃書，自陳誣枉，妃父衍不敢以聞。
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.en: At Xu the heir apparent wrote to his consort proclaiming his innocence; her father Wang Yan did not dare report it.
fullGoverningChineseAndPairedEnglish.literal: When the Heir Apparent reached Xu he sent a letter to the consort stating his false accusation; the consort's father Yan did not dare report it.
